Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for renewal — initial numbers

Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Renewal for our Dedicated pool comes up April 1 and we need to nail the sizing before the renewal proposal. Attached is our Q4 token/seq distribution and average active sessions per hour. Short summary:

- Peak sustained concurrent sessions: ~220 language-generation sessions per hour (95th percentile).
- Median sequence length: 520 tokens; 95th percentile: 1,800 tokens.
- Current Dedicated allocation: 8x A100 GPUs in our Redwood pool; observed average GPU utilization: 68% over last 90 days, with 3 big spikes hitting 95% lasting ~30–45 minutes.

We want recommendations for: 1) minimal guaranteed capacity to avoid throttling during renewal, 2) a realistic burst plan (how many extra GPUs, and cost model), and 3) whether resizing mid-term is feasible if utilization drops/rises.

Can you confirm what telemetry you need to produce a sizing and a quick plan? I attached usage_report_Q4.csv. Procurement may be looped in after we have an OK on the sizing and estimated monthly commit.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

Priya — thanks for the data. That usage profile lines up with what I expected. A few quick notes and a proposal for next steps: 

1) Telemetry: the CSV is perfect. If you can add a short extract of per-request latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and a distribution of sequence lengths by endpoint, that will let us pick a quantization and batch strategy.

2) Near-term sizing options (high-level):
   - Option A (conservative): Increase to 12x A100s (add 4 GPUs). This targets 85–90% steady util under expected Q2 growth and keeps p95 latency under 1.2s for your median requests.
   - Option B (cost-conscious): Keep at 8x A100s + enable burst pool of up to 6 GPUs (pay-as-you-go). This lowers committed cost but requires work to wire burst policies into your CloudOps runbook.

3) Resizing cadence: We support mid-contract resizing on monthly checkpoints (with 14-day notice) and immediate short-term burst capacity for spikes. For mid-term downward resizing, we usually recommend a 30–60 day observation window to avoid oscillation.

4) Deliverables: I’ll run a sizing calc and send a proposal with estimated monthly committed cost, burst pricing, and expected latency impact. I attached our capacity plan template to make it easier to map to your procurement cycle.

Can we schedule a 30-min call next week to review the calc? I’ll pull Rishi in — he’ll have the kernel-level perf numbers.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Hi Priya / Marissa — looping in Grace (our account lead) and Dev (infra engineering).

I ran a few back-of-envelope calcs based on the CSV and a short kernel profile from Dev. Key assumptions:
- Model: 70B decoder-only (attention memory scales with seq length).
- Average tokens generated per request: ~420 (after prompt).
- Effective batchable concurrency given your latency targets: ~6–8 requests per GPU slot.

Projected capacity needs (95th percentile peak):
- Baseline sustained: 8 GPUs will generally cover median load but leaves only ~10–15% headroom for spikes.
- Recommended committed pool: 12 GPUs (satisfies peak with 75–80% avg util, single-digit p99 tail improvement).
- Burst pool for headroom: configure 4 additional GPUs as burst. If spikes go beyond 4 GPUs, route to hosted fallback models (lower-cost third-party variants) to preserve latency SLAs.

Cost delta (rough): committed 8 -> 12: +50% monthly commit; burst usage estimated 8–12% of hours based on recent spikes. I'll attach a notebook with the calcs. If you prefer smaller commit, Option B (8 committed + 6 burst) is viable but requires emergency routing rules to avoid queueing.

On resizing: we can automate monthly checkpoints. Dev: can we provide an automated utilization report that flags sustained >80% util for 7 days?

—Rishi
